dependency: R1 recirculation fan operating through the return duct

predictions.account: Hypothesis: station moisture travels through the return duct back to the loop, subsequently reaches the station through supply, and promotes curling. The proposed causal arrow is return-mediated moisture exposure to label curl.
predictions.when: Proposed comparison: alternate return-damper-open and return-damper-closed intervals using R2 while R1 remains on and the supply grille remains open. Hold batch arrival rate, handoff window, original label identities, and footprint fixed; seek the same valued outcome in every interval. Record damper and fan state with M4, humidity with R4/M2, curl fraction with M1, and scanner reads and timing with R3/M3. Check whether supply delivery changes before interpreting the contrast.
predictions.result: If the return-mediated account dominates and supply delivery and other relevant conditions remain comparable, closing the return link should reduce subsequent station humidity exposure and curl fraction relative to open intervals. Restoring the link should restore the tendency after a possible lag. This is a prediction, not an observed successful intervention or proof that the return link is necessary.

predictions.account: Rival hypothesis with reversed causal attribution: label contact with a moist station surface produces curl, and the same local moisture subsequently enters the return duct. Return-path moisture is downstream of the local cause rather than the cause of curling.
predictions.when: Use the same proposed return-only damper comparison at fixed initial demand, identity requirements, handoff window, footprint, and intended legibility outcome. As a separate proposed contrast, use R5 to hold labels away from the surface while holding fan and damper states fixed and checking scanner reads and timing.
predictions.result: If surface contact dominates and the damper comparison leaves surface exposure comparable, return closure should leave curl fraction substantially unchanged even if the humidity trace changes. Holding labels away from the surface should reduce curl at unchanged return state. Neither result has been observed; both depend on the stated comparability conditions and could still admit other mechanisms.

predictions.account: Rival hypothesis: an unmeasured environmental variable controls curl susceptibility and explains the protected fan-on, curl-free anomaly.
predictions.when: Repeat the proposed fixed-arrival, fixed-window open/closed return comparisons across multiple intervals, retaining O4 as an unexplained observation and comparing the recorded humidity and state traces without treating them as exhaustive environmental measurements.
predictions.result: Curl may vary across intervals without a reproducible damper-state response, including further fan-on intervals without curl. Such findings would weaken a deterministic return-link account but would not identify the hidden variable; absence of curl in O4 already prevents treating fan operation as sufficient evidence for curling.

surviving_outcome: Valued outcome to preserve under the proposed return-link intervention: keep the labeled batch legible at the handoff station without missing the stipulated handoff window. Only intact-label scanner readability when the fan is manually stopped is stipulated as observed; preservation of the full valued outcome under return closure remains a hypothesis. That observed readability challenges an assumed necessity of fan operation for scanning, but supplies no observed causal direction for curling or proof of timely handoff across all arrivals.
unknowns: No return-only intervention has been logged; the observed fan-stop scanner result changes more than the return link and cannot establish return-link necessity or causal direction.
Damper closure may alter supply delivery or station pressure despite leaving the supply grille open; the available observations do not establish that these are held comparable.

Whether station moisture follows the return link or follows label contact with the surface remains unresolved; a station humidity trace does not directly trace moisture through the complete circulation path.
The hidden conditions producing the protected fan-on, curl-free O4 interval remain unknown, and no mechanism is proved.
Whether fan-free construction or the proposed return closure preserves legibility and the fixed handoff window across all stipulated arrivals remains unproved.
